C-SYSTEMONE-DECISION-BACKEND.Summary: Introduce a provider-neutral System One decision client that speaks the de-facto POST /v1/systemone protocol (noul, choice, score) over a configurable base URL, add an optional canonical systemone connection section and a systemone plugin toggle, and add guardian.decisionBackend ("fast" | "systemone") so Guardian resolves its bounded low-risk assessment either through the current snapshot-bound fast auxiliary model or through a calibrated decision provider, with an explicit shadow-calibration mode, fail-closed fallback to the existing fast path, credential-safe ${VAR} key resolution, and no live network in the repository gate.
C-SYSTEMONE-DECISION-BACKEND.Problem: Guardian currently derives its low-risk verdict by asking the captured fast-role auxiliary model to emit free-form JSON that is then parsed and thresholded. A calibrated System One decision provider returns typed, schema-exact answers with probabilities, is cheaper and faster for high-frequency permission review, and cannot be steered into emitting malicious prose. However, binding Guardian directly to a single vendor would create lock-in: the decision-model ecosystem has converged on the de-facto POST /v1/systemone protocol, served by hosted Jev, open models, local servers, and gateways, while OpenAI Decisions API and Alibaba/Qwen decision products use their own, currently non-public, wire shapes. The correct unit to bind is therefore the protocol class, not one vendor or model. There is also no safe way today to calibrate such a provider against Guardian's real decisions before it becomes authoritative.

Goals.Goal: Add a provider-neutral System One client that issues POST {baseUrl}/v1/systemone with {model, state, questions} and decodes typed noul, choice, and score answers with their probabilities and confidence, tolerating and ignoring unknown response fields per the protocol contract.

Add an optional strict canonical top-level systemone section carrying connection settings (baseUrl, model, optional ${VAR} apiKey, timeoutMs, maxRetries, enabled) so any compliant endpoint — hosted Jev, a gateway, or a local server such as Ollama, laya-serve, or Kev — is selected by configuration alone with no vendor-specific code path.
Extend guardian with decisionBackend ("fast" | "systemone") defaulting to "fast" so the existing behavior is byte-for-byte preserved unless the operator opts in.

Let the systemone backend derive the same bounded Guardian assessment by asking two typed questions over the existing review state: a noul for whether the planned action is low-risk (read-only or reversible, touches no secrets, stays within the repository) and a score for risk on an ordered rubric, mapping the results onto the existing risk_level and risk_score shape.

Add an explicit shadow-calibration mode in which the systemone provider is evaluated and logged but the fast backend remains authoritative, so thresholds can be measured against real decisions before the provider is trusted.

Keep all Guardian guarantees intact when the systemone backend is active: auto-approval only for an explicit low verdict under approvalRiskThreshold, never overriding deny or explicit allow, and deferring on every uncertainty, error, timeout, or invalid answer.
Fail closed to the fast backend, never to a guess, when the systemone provider is disabled, unconfigured, unreachable, times out, or returns answers outside the required noul and score primitives.

Resolve systemone.apiKey from a ${VAR} placeholder through the existing env-substitution contract, keep it out of persisted config snapshots, logs, and diagnostics, and disable the provider with a value-free diagnostic when the placeholder is unset or empty.
Add a systemone plugin toggle that, when disabled, constructs no provider and forces Guardian onto the fast backend, as a kill switch for network, cost, or privacy concerns.

Keep the canonical embedded schema, schemas/vvoc/v3.json, module contracts, README, package exports, GRACE graph, and GRACE verification synchronized with the implemented behavior, and never edit generated dist output.

Constraints.Constraint: Configuration stays strict canonical schema v3: the systemone section and the guardian extension are optional, every previously valid config remains valid, and the embedded schema matches schemas/vvoc/v3.json exactly.

The protocol binding is the de-facto /v1/systemone shape (state plus typed questions; noul, choice, score) and never a vendor brand: no jev-only field or behavior is required, and unknown response fields are ignored.
Only noul and score are required for this change; choice is decoded but unused, and an endpoint that cannot answer noul and score is treated as unavailable rather than partially trusted.

Guardian's default decisionBackend remains "fast" with identical behavior; opting into systemone is explicit, and an unbound, disabled, or misconfigured provider always defers to manual approval via the existing fail-closed path.
Shadow mode never mutates the permission effect: when shadow is enabled the fast backend is authoritative and the systemone evaluation is observational and logging-only.
No implicit cloud endpoint: baseUrl and model must be configured explicitly; the change ships no default that silently sends repository or transcript content to a hosted service.
Runtime plugins share the startup config snapshot, so systemone and guardian changes require an OpenCode restart, consistent with every existing runtime plugin.

The apiKey placeholder is resolved through M-ENV-SUBSTITUTION and protected by M-PLUGIN-SECRETS-REDACTION; the raw key and the request state are bounded in diagnostics and never written to logs or persisted snapshots.

Network effects are bounded: a finite request timeout, a finite retry count with no unbounded retry loop, and per-decision failure containment so a decision-provider outage cannot destabilize the host or block permission handling.

Verification is deterministic and injectable: tests use an injected transport and injected Guardian dependencies and must not require a real endpoint, API key, network, or live model call; a live-endpoint walkthrough is a documented manual step only.
OpenAI Decisions API and Alibaba/Qwen decision adapters are out of scope for this change because their request and response schemas are not public; adding a third wire shape now would be guessing.
Source contracts, README, canonical schema, GRACE graph, and GRACE verification state remain synchronized with the implemented behavior, and no generated dist output is edited manually.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Do not implement an OpenAI Decisions API adapter or a Qwen/Alibaba decision adapter in this change; they are deferred until a public schema exists.
Do not use a System One provider as an OpenCode model, provider, or vv-role for generation; it returns decisions, not text or code.
Do not add any other System One consumer besides Guardian: no tool-history pruning, reviewer cascade, skill routing, model routing, semantic spec lint, or evidence checking in this change.
Do not let System One decide acceptance, review verdicts, scope, or content; it only supplies a signal to deterministic code that owns the threshold and the consequence.
Do not build calibration datasets, fitting, or threshold-search tooling; shadow mode only records comparable decisions for later manual calibration.
Do not introduce a multi-provider registry, per-consumer shadow policies, or a capability matrix beyond the required noul and score primitives in this change.
Do not default to, or hard-code, any hosted endpoint, model name, or vendor alias as an implicit path.
Do not change the fast auxiliary backend's model, role resolution, timeout semantics, or prompt contract.
Do not use a live System One endpoint, API key, or live model provider as a repository verification gate.
Do not add a new process, CLI command, or MCP server in this change; the client is an in-process library used by Guardian.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The System One client sends POST {baseUrl}/v1/systemone with a JSON body containing model, state, and a questions map, and decodes noul, choice, and score answers with probabilities and confidence while ignoring unknown response fields, proven with an injected transport.

The top-level optional systemone section validates enabled, baseUrl, model, apiKey, timeoutMs, and maxRetries; baseUrl and model are required when the section is present; the embedded schema equals schemas/vvoc/v3.json; and every previously valid config remains valid.
Guardian with decisionBackend "fast" (the default) produces the same decisions and side effects as before the change, confirmed by the existing Guardian tests passing unchanged.

Guardian with decisionBackend "systemone" derives risk_level and risk_score from a noul low-risk question and a score risk rubric over the existing bounded review state, and reuses the existing low-level-and-below-threshold auto-approval rule.

With decisionBackend "systemone" and shadow enabled, the systemone provider is evaluated and a structured comparison is logged, but the permission effect is determined solely by the fast backend and is never mutated by the observed systemone answer.

When the provider is disabled, unconfigured, unreachable, times out, or returns a missing or unsupported noul or score, Guardian defers to manual approval through the existing fail-closed path and never auto-approves.
The systemone plugin toggle, when disabled, constructs no provider and forces the fast backend; toggling it off never breaks permission handling.

systemone.apiKey is resolved from a ${VAR} placeholder, is absent from persisted config snapshots and from every log or diagnostic, and an unset or empty placeholder disables the provider with a value-free warning.

Switching between a hosted endpoint and a local endpoint is a baseUrl and model change only, with no vendor-specific branch, proven by a test that exercises at least two distinct base URLs through the same client.
The provider applies the configured timeout and a bounded retry count, and a provider outage or slow response cannot throw out of the permission hook or block other permission evaluations.
Focused Guardian, System One client, config, and toggle tests pass together with the repository check, build, pack, and GRACE gates; no test requires a live endpoint, API key, or live model call.
Module contracts, README, canonical schema, package exports, GRACE graph, and GRACE verification are updated to match the implemented behavior, and no generated dist output is edited.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/lib/systemone.test.ts src/lib/vvoc-config.test.ts src/lib/plugin-toggle-config.test.ts src/plugins/guardian/index.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh deterministic output proves: request shaping and typed noul, choice, and score decoding with unknown fields ignored, over an injected transport; strict acceptance and rejection of the optional systemone section with the embedded schema equal to schemas/vvoc/v3.json and previously valid configs still valid; unchanged Guardian behavior under the default fast backend; systemone-backed derivation of risk_level and risk_score with the existing low-and-below-threshold rule; shadow mode evaluating systemone without mutating the permission effect; fail-closed deferral on disabled, unconfigured, unreachable, timed-out, and malformed answers; the systemone toggle forcing the fast backend; ${VAR} key resolution with the key absent from snapshots, logs, and diagnostics and a value-free warning when unset; two distinct base URLs exercised through one client with no vendor branch; bounded timeout and retry with no throw escaping the permission hook. No live endpoint, API key, network, or live model call is used, and any live walkthrough is documented as a manual step.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user chose to bind to the protocol class rather than to Jev specifically: the systemone name and section are canonical, the provider is selected by baseUrl and model, and the default decisionBackend remains fast. OpenAI and Qwen adapters are explicitly deferred.

The de-facto /v1/systemone protocol (state plus typed questions with noul, choice, and score) is stable enough to implement against its published draft; unknown response fields are ignored and provider-specific extras do not change the client contract.

Hosted Jev (for example https://api.typesafe.ai with model jev-latest), gateway routes, and local servers such as Ollama, laya-serve, and Kev all serve compatible noul and score answers; if a target endpoint does not, it is simply treated as unavailable and Guardian falls back to fast.

Guardian's bounded review state (policy prompt plus planned action plus bounded host transcript) fits the provider's context budget, and the existing truncation guarantees are reused; if a provider has a smaller context, the existing bounded rendering remains authoritative and no spec requirement changes.

Guardian's inference dependency is already injectable (policy, history, infer, log), so the systemone backend is added as an alternative implementation of the same seam without changing the handler's decision contract.

A provider that answers noul and score but not choice, or vice versa, is acceptable because this change only requires noul and score; capability enumeration is a deferred decision recorded in the design context.
